features.sub: The decisions that shaped the product. If any of them stop being true, that's a bug worth filing.

0.h: Ten focused tools. The essentials, covered.
0.p: Tools cover the everyday work: inbox_list, email_read (list, read, search) and email_compose (send, reply), plus focused tools for organizing, deleting, folders, drafts, scheduling, contacts, and signatures. Paste the MCP endpoint URL into claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible agent.

1.h: Email is fetched live. Never stored.
1.p: Every tool call hits your provider in real time: Gmail API, Fastmail JMAP, or IMAP. Message bodies, subjects, and attachments go to the agent and are discarded immediately. We persist one thing per inbox, an encrypted token or app password, so we can make the next call. The one exception is a message you schedule to send later: we hold it until the send time, then keep a record for your history.

2.h: You stay in control of every send.
2.p: Messages go through Gmail, Fastmail, or your own SMTP server, never our mail relay. Turn on per-inbox approval to hold sends, replies, forwards, draft sends, and scheduled sends for dashboard review. Automated retries can reuse an idempotency key for 24 hours, and Gmail can send only from a provider-verified Send As identity.

3.h: Gmail, iCloud, Fastmail & any IMAP inbox.
3.p: OAuth 2.0 for Gmail; app-specific passwords for Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, and Yandex; a generic IMAP / SMTP connector for everything else. Every inbox reports a versioned compatibility profile, so an agent can use portable actions while seeing where a provider behaves differently or cannot support an operation.

4.h: OAuth 2.0 for agents. One click to revoke.
4.p: We're standard MCP (streamable-http) with OAuth 2.1, DCR & PKCE, so there is no vendor lock-in. Works with Claude, Cursor, VS Code, ChatGPT, Windsurf, n8n, Make, LibreChat, OpenWebUI, and any MCP-compatible client. OAuth clients connect automatically via authorization code + PKCE; a scoped API key covers clients without OAuth and scripted access. Revoke any connection from the dashboard in one click.

5.p: OAuth tokens and app passwords are AES-256-GCM encrypted before being written to the database. Decryption happens only inside an isolated Edge Function at call time. The encryption key is stored as an environment secret, separate from the database.

howItWorks.title: You're the user. We're the pipe.
howItWorks.sub: Three steps from sign-up to your agent reading and sending mail.

0.p: Sign in and click Connect Inbox. Choose Gmail, iCloud, Fastmail, or any IMAP inbox, then complete OAuth or paste an app password. Credentials are encrypted; the mail your agent reads is never stored.

1.h: Paste the URL: OAuth or API key
1.p: For an MCP client that supports OAuth 2.0 (claude.ai, Claude Desktop, Cursor, and others), paste https://mcpemails.com/api/mcp, click Connect, and authorize. No key needed. For clients without OAuth (Cline, JetBrains, custom scripts), generate a scoped API key in the dashboard instead.

2.p: The agent calls tools like email_read() or email_compose(). MCPEmails fetches live from your provider and returns the result. Nothing is cached between calls.

tools.0: Discover all connected inboxes and their IDs. Call this first, no UUID copy-pasting from the dashboard.
tools.1: Read mail: list recent summaries, fetch a full message, batch-read up to 50, search across providers, extract readable attachment text, or save the original email as .eml.
tools.2: Organize mail: move, copy, delete, flag, or archive, whether one at a time, in bulk, or straight from a search. Long bulk runs report their status and can be cancelled from the dashboard.
tools.3: Compose: send a new message, reply in-thread, or forward through Gmail API, Fastmail JMAP, or SMTP. Optional inbox approval holds outbound mail for dashboard review before it leaves.
tools.4: Manage folders (labels on Gmail): list, create, rename, or delete, and use them as move destinations.
tools.5: Drafts: list, create, update, and send provider-stored drafts, including an unsent reply kept in the source conversation for review.
tools.6: Schedule a message for a future time, list pending scheduled sends, and cancel them before they go out.
tools.7: Find people by name or email with a live scan of recent matching mail. Nothing is stored.

examples.sub: No dashboards to learn. Tell your AI assistant what you want in plain English, and it uses mcpemails to get it done.

quote.text: I wanted my agents to work my inbox, but every option meant handing a third party a copy of my email. So I built the pipe I wished existed: connect once, your inbox is fetched live and never stored, and you can cut off any agent in a click. That's the product I trust with my own inbox.

faq.title: Questions, answered
faq.sub: Everything you need to know before connecting your first inbox.

items.a: We use privacy-preserving, cookieless product analytics to understand site and setup performance. We never collect email content, addresses, API keys, OAuth tokens, or MCP request data.

items.q: Which AI clients does it work with?
items.a: Any MCP-compatible client. We're a standard streamable-http MCP server with OAuth 2.1, DCR and PKCE, so the same inbox works in Claude, Cursor, VS Code, ChatGPT, Windsurf, n8n, Make, LibreChat and more. Paste one endpoint URL and you're connected, with no per-app rebuild.

items.q: Which email providers can I connect?
items.a: Gmail over OAuth (one click), Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho and Yandex with an app-specific password, and any other mailbox over a generic IMAP/SMTP connection. Connect as many inboxes as you like and label them by use case.

No. The mail your agent reads is fetched live from your provider on each request and never stored on our servers. The only exception is a message you explicitly schedule to send later, which is held encrypted until it goes out.

Yes. The free plan connects one inbox, forever, with no card required, and your agent gets every tool we ship against it: read, search, send, reply, schedule and organise. Personal is $5 a month for a second and third mailbox on the same agent, Pro removes the inbox limit entirely, and Team is for when other people need in.

items.q: What can the AI actually do with my inbox?
items.a: Read and search mail, send, reply and forward real messages, schedule sends for later, and organize your inbox: move, copy, flag, archive and delete. Nine action-based tools, so the agent finishes the job inside your inbox instead of just drafting.

items.q: How do I connect an inbox?
items.a: Create a free account, connect your mailbox (one click for Gmail, or paste an app password for the others), then drop https://mcpemails.com/api/mcp into your AI client and authorize. Your agent has the inbox in a couple of minutes.

Yes. MCP Emails is open source under AGPL-3.0, and the hosted service runs the same server you can run yourself. A docker-compose stack gets the full MCP server and all its tools running against your own database in about five minutes, for any IMAP or SMTP mailbox. Gmail and Outlook one-click OAuth and the dashboard stay on the hosted plan.
